recipes.name: Enchiladas inspired by Schitt's Creek
ingredients: 3 large cooked chicken breasts from salsa roja, shredded
3 poblano peppers, halved and fire roasted
8 oz queso de papa cheddar, shredded
Additional queso de papa, for topping
instructions: For the Salsa Roja
Start by removing the stems and seeds from the chilis and cut into 1” segments. - Cherry red guajillo chilis - Dried ancho chilis - Pasilla chilis (optional)
Peel and medium onions into chunks. Cut plum tomatoes in half. Peel the cloves of garlic. - 2 medium onions peeled and chopped - 2 plum tomatoes halved - 3 cloves garlic peeled
Over the stovetop, dry roast the peppers in a dry pan over medium heat for 1-2 minutes. Set aside once roasted.

Into the same pan goes the onions, garlic, and tomatoes to char a little bit. Once the onions and tomatoes have picked up a little color, add back in the chiles along with enough water to cover everything in the pot. - Water
Bring to a bare simmer, then add in a generous pinch of Mexican oregano. - Mexican oregano (optional)
Take large chicken breasts and butterfly cut each piece before killing the heat and adding the chicken to the pot of vegetables, making sure to fully submerge the chicken. - 3 large chicken breasts
Once nestled, cover and let sit for 15 minutes before removing the chicken when it has reached an internal temperature of 164°F.

In a blender, add in the vegetables and chiles before covering just enough with the cooking liquid. Blend until a canned tomato sauce consistency is reached. Season with a few pinches of kosher salt and twists of freshly ground pepper to taste. - Freshly ground black pepper - Kosher salt
Blend one last time to combine.
for the Enchilada Filling and Assembly:

Start by shredding the large chicken breasts from the red sauce. Remove the stems and seeds of poblano peppers and cut in half. - 3 large cooked chicken breasts from salsa roja shredded - 3 poblano peppers halved and fire roasted

Place each half of the poblano pepper over the stovetop and roast until the exteriors are fully blackened. After the pepper is fully roasted, pile them together onto aluminum foil and wrap the peppers up into a package.
Using gloved hands, scrape off all of the blackened exteriors and slice into small pieces.
For the Queso

In a pot add flour and butter. Cook and whisk together for 1-2 minutes over low heat. Slowly stream in whole milk while constantly whisking until a thick white sauce has formed. - 3 tbsp butter - 3 tbsp flour - 2 cups whole milk

Kill the heat, add in shredded queso de papa and, using a rubber spatula, gently fold in the cheese (stirring gently from the bottom upward over the cheese) until smooth. - 8 oz queso de papa cheddar shredded
For the Corn tortillas

In a saucepan filled with a little vegetable oil over medium heat fry, each tortilla for just a few seconds on each side. Once fried, drain on paper towels. Rinse and repeat with a dozen more tortillas. - Corn tortillas - Vegetable oil
for the Assembly
Start by preparing a dipping and rolling station along with an optional Oaxaca cheese. - Oaxaca Cheese
Pour some Salsa Roja into a shallow dish then dip and thoroughly coat a tortilla on both sides with Salsa Roja. - For the Salsa Roja - for the Corn tortillas

Layer with shredded chicken, Oaxaca cheese, and poblano peppers in the center of the tortilla before rolling the tortilla around tightly. - large cooked chicken breasts from salsa roja shredded - Oaxaca Cheese - poblano peppers halved and fire roasted
Place the seam side down in a waiting pre-oiled casserole dish. Rinse and repeat until the casserole dish is full.

Generously drizzle the tortillas with more salsa Roja and topping with more shredded queso de papa then finishing off with a generous drizzle of the cheese sauce. - For the Salsa Roja - Additional queso de papa for topping - for the Corn tortillas
Place into a preheated 400°F oven uncovered for 10-15 minutes or until lightly brown and bubbly.
Let rest at room temperature for 10 minutes before serving.
